cues: The older open hearth, or Siemens Martin process, uses a shallow hearth heated by producer gas, with brick regenerators that recycle the heat.
The oxidising agent is haematite added to the charge, which burns out carbon, silicon, manganese and phosphorus.
It is slow, eight to ten hours, but the operator can sample and adjust the melt, so alloy and tool steels are still made this way.
